review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. Owner decision 2 (2026-10-06): Niebla is not used as the core of the bridge; the plan's Niebla slot is taken by this new course-authored unit (or by a library text that ladder:place shows readable at that point). A contemporary conversation with voseo between two friends (Ana, Karla) and market vendors (usted): the supply the plan's section 4 says the open library lacks. Points for the Honduran reviewer: "regatear", "va pues", "cabal", "mi niña", "doña", "¿A cómo...?", "libra", "centavos", prices in lempiras (invented and probably too round), "chiquitines" (cipotes is more Honduran; kept because the lemma helps Galdós), "yuca", "aguacates", "carro", "leña / carbón / estufa", "vos" as an interjection ("ya compramos la piña, vos"), voseo forms (querés, Mirá, Llevá, Fijate). Owner decision 3: the 92 % entry line for authentic placements stays; new-lemmas warnings are acceptable. Vocabulary plan: Not in PLAN-B1 as written: this unit takes the plan's Niebla slot es-b1-29 (Niebla ch09). Its vocabulary is a market and party lexicon chosen for coverage of Martí and Galdós (gordo, fino, miel, madera, sacos, fama, ay, inteligente, chiquitín, ...). Logged.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Mañana es el cumpleaños de Nico, y Ana y Karla van a la plaza a comprar todo para la fiesta.
sentences.english: Tomorrow is Nico's birthday, and Ana and Karla are going to the square to buy everything for the party.

sentences.text: Karla tiene una lista larga en la mano, y Ana se ríe cuando la ve.
sentences.english: Karla has a long list in her hand, and Ana laughs when she sees it.

sentences.text: —¿Todo eso querés comprar, Karla? —pregunta Ana.
sentences.english: "Is that everything you want to buy, Karla?" asks Ana.

sentences.text: —Sí, y todavía falta lo más importante: el pastel —contesta Karla.
sentences.english: "Yes, and the most important thing is still missing: the cake," answers Karla.

sentences.text: —Nico cumple diez años, y no quiero que nadie se quede sin comer.
sentences.english: "Nico turns ten, and I do not want anybody to go without food."

sentences.text: —Mirá, vamos primero al mercado, y después hacemos las cuentas con calma —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "Look, let's go to the market first, and then we'll do the sums calmly," says Ana.

sentences.text: —Llevá dinero en billetes pequeños, porque en la plaza nadie tiene cambio —le recuerda Ana.
sentences.english: "Take money in small notes, because nobody in the square has change," Ana reminds her.

sentences.text: Ana lleva una canasta grande, y Karla lleva la lista y las monedas.
sentences.english: Ana carries a big basket, and Karla carries the list and the coins.

sentences.text: La canasta está vacía, pero Ana ya sabe que al volver la canasta va a pesar mucho.
sentences.english: The basket is empty, but Ana already knows that on the way back the basket will be heavy.

sentences.text: Salen temprano, antes de que el sol caliente el pueblo.
sentences.english: They set out early, before the sun heats up the town.

sentences.text: La plaza está llena de gente y de gritos.
sentences.english: The square is full of people and shouts.

sentences.text: En el mercado hay de todo: ropa, ollas, flores y hasta animales.
sentences.english: In the market there is everything: clothes, pots, flowers and even animals.

sentences.text: Una vendedora grita: «¡Aguacates, aguacates!», y otra ofrece yuca fresca y chile.
sentences.english: A vendor shouts: "Avocados, avocados!", and another offers yuca and chilli.

sentences.text: Ana se detiene en un puesto y mira las piñas.
sentences.english: Ana stops at a stall and looks at the pineapples.

sentences.text: —Buenos días, doña —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "Good morning, ma'am," says Ana.

sentences.text: ¿A cómo está la piña?
sentences.english: "How much is the pineapple?"

sentences.text: —A veinte lempiras la piña, mi niña, y es dulce como la miel —contesta la vendedora.
sentences.english: "Twenty lempiras for the pineapple, dear, and it is sweet as honey," answers the vendor.

sentences.text: —Ay, veinte, ¿tan caro? —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "Oh, twenty, so dear?" says Ana.

sentences.text: —La semana pasada estaba a quince.
sentences.english: "Last week it was fifteen."

sentences.text: —Es que llovió mucho, y la cosecha vino pequeña —explica la vendedora.
sentences.english: "It's just that it rained a lot, and the harvest came in small," explains the vendor.

sentences.text: Ana mira a Karla y sonríe, porque Karla ya sabe lo que viene: Ana va a regatear.
sentences.english: Ana looks at Karla and smiles, because Karla already knows what is coming: Ana is going to haggle.

sentences.text: En la plaza, regatear no es una falta de respeto, sino una costumbre.
sentences.english: In the square, haggling is not disrespect but a custom.

sentences.text: —Mire, doña, si llevo tres piñas, ¿me hace un descuento?
sentences.english: "Look, ma'am, if I take three pineapples, will you give me a discount?"

sentences.text: —Tres piñas, cuarenta y cinco —dice la vendedora.
sentences.english: "Three pineapples, forty-five," says the vendor.

sentences.text: —Cuarenta, y le compro también una docena de limones —contesta Ana.
sentences.english: "Forty, and I'll also buy a dozen lemons from you," answers Ana.

sentences.text: La rebaja es poca, pero la docena de limones vale la pena.
sentences.english: The reduction is small, but the dozen lemons are worth it.

sentences.text: —Cuarenta y dos, y no digamos más, porque ya me quedé sin ganancia —dice la vendedora.
sentences.english: "Forty-two, and let's say no more, because I've already lost my profit," says the vendor.

sentences.text: —Va pues, cuarenta y dos —acepta Ana.
sentences.english: "All right, forty-two," agrees Ana.

sentences.text: Karla paga con billetes grandes, y la vendedora le da el cambio en monedas.
sentences.english: Karla pays with big notes, and the vendor gives her the change in coins.

sentences.text: Entre las monedas hay unos centavos, y Karla se queda mirándolos en la mano.
sentences.english: Among the coins there are a few cents, and Karla stands looking at them in her hand.

sentences.text: Son centavos de los viejos, y casi nadie los acepta ya.
sentences.english: They are the old cents, and almost nobody accepts them any more.

sentences.text: Los centavos casi no valen nada, pero la vendedora los cuenta uno por uno.
sentences.english: The cents are worth almost nothing, but the vendor counts them one by one.

sentences.text: —¿Y los aguacates, doña?
sentences.english: "And the avocados, ma'am?"

sentences.text: ¿A cómo están los aguacates?
sentences.english: "How much are the avocados?"

sentences.text: —A cinco lempiras cada uno, y son de los buenos —dice la vendedora.
sentences.english: "Five lempiras each, and they are good ones," says the vendor.

sentences.text: —Si me da seis aguacates y una libra de yuca, ¿me hace una rebaja? —pregunta Ana.
sentences.english: "If you give me six avocados and a pound of yuca, will you give me a reduction?" asks Ana.

sentences.text: —Está bien, le hago la rebaja, pero no se lo cuente a nadie —contesta la señora.
sentences.english: "All right, I'll give you the reduction, but don't tell anybody," answers the woman.

sentences.text: Karla se ríe, porque las dos saben que la señora le hace la misma rebaja a todo el mundo.
sentences.english: Karla laughs, because the two of them know that the woman gives everyone the same reduction.

sections.title: Naranjas, huevos y un pollo gordo

sentences.text: En el siguiente puesto, Ana pide naranjas, y esta vez no regatea tanto.
sentences.english: At the next stall Ana asks for oranges, and this time she does not haggle as much.

sentences.text: —Dos docenas de naranjas, por favor, para el jugo de mañana —pide Ana.
sentences.english: "Two dozen oranges, please, for tomorrow's juice," Ana asks.

sentences.text: —Mirá que el jugo no alcanza si son sólo naranjas —le dice Karla en voz baja.
sentences.english: "Look, the juice won't be enough if it's only oranges," Karla says to her in a low voice.

sentences.text: —Entonces compramos también mango para el jugo, ¿no? —propone Ana.
sentences.english: "Then we'll buy mango for the juice as well, won't we?" proposes Ana.

sentences.text: —Ya compramos la piña, vos —le dice Karla.
sentences.english: "We already bought the pineapple, you know," Karla tells her.

sentences.text: —Es verdad, ay, qué cabeza la mía —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "That's true, oh, what a head I have," says Ana.

sentences.text: Se ríen las dos, y la vendedora de naranjas se ríe también.
sentences.english: The two of them laugh, and the orange seller laughs too.

sentences.text: Compran un mango maduro, y la vendedora lo pesa en la mano.
sentences.english: They buy a ripe mango, and the vendor weighs it in her hand.

sentences.text: —Mango fino, doña, de los que sólo se encuentran un día por semana —dice la vendedora.
sentences.english: "Fine mango, ma'am, the kind you only find one day a week," says the vendor.

sentences.text: Siguen caminando hasta un puesto donde una señora vende huevos.
sentences.english: They keep walking until a stall where a woman sells eggs.

sentences.text: Esta señora tiene fama de vender los mejores huevos del mercado.
sentences.english: This woman has a reputation for selling the best eggs in the market.

sentences.text: —Una docena de huevos, y que sean grandes, por favor —dice Karla.
sentences.english: "A dozen eggs, and make them big ones, please," says Karla.

sentences.text: —Para la gente de la clínica, lo mejor que tengo —contesta la señora de los huevos.
sentences.english: "For the people of the clinic, the best I have," answers the egg woman.

sentences.text: —Por algo tiene usted tanta fama, doña —le dice Ana.
sentences.english: "No wonder you have such a reputation, ma'am," Ana tells her.

sentences.text: —La fama no se compra, mi niña: se gana con los años, y a veces la fama pesa más que los huevos.
sentences.english: "A reputation is not bought, dear: you earn it over the years, and sometimes the reputation weighs more than the eggs."

sentences.text: —¿Y el pollo? —pregunta Ana.
sentences.english: "And the chicken?" asks Ana.

sentences.text: ¿Cuánto cuesta el pollo gordo?
sentences.english: "How much is the fat chicken?"

sentences.text: —A treinta lempiras la libra, mi niña, y ese pollo es fino, no es de esos delgados.
sentences.english: "Thirty lempiras a pound, dear, and that chicken is a fine one, not one of those thin ones."

sentences.text: Karla piensa en cuántas personas van a venir mañana y hace una cuenta rápida con los dedos.
sentences.english: Karla thinks about how many people are coming tomorrow and does a quick sum on her fingers.

sentences.text: —Dos pollos gordos son seis libras, y cada libra a treinta, son ciento ochenta.
sentences.english: "Two fat chickens are six pounds, and at thirty a pound, that is a hundred and eighty."

sentences.text: Ana dice que sí con la cabeza, pone dos pollos en la canasta y regatea otra vez, sin prisa.
sentences.english: Ana nods, puts two chickens in the basket and haggles again, without hurrying.

sentences.text: —Si me lleva los dos pollos gordos, ¿me da un descuento de diez lempiras? —pregunta Ana.
sentences.english: "If you take both fat chickens, will you give me a discount of ten lempiras?" asks Ana.

sentences.text: —Cabal, diez lempiras, y le regalo una bolsita de chile —dice la señora.
sentences.english: "Right then, ten lempiras, and I'll give you a little bag of chilli," says the woman.

sentences.text: —Cabal, doña, pero que el chile sea del bueno —contesta Ana.
sentences.english: "Right, ma'am, but make sure the chilli is a good one," answers Ana.

sentences.text: —Cabal, mi niña, cabal —ríe la señora.
sentences.english: "Right, dear, right," laughs the woman.

sentences.text: —Entonces, trato hecho —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "Then it's a deal," says Ana.

sentences.text: Para la comida de mañana necesitan fuego, y hay que comprar leña.
sentences.english: For tomorrow's meal they need fire, and they have to buy firewood.

sentences.text: Al final de la plaza hay un hombre con un carro lleno de leña y de sacos de carbón.
sentences.english: At the end of the square there is a man with a car full of firewood and sacks of charcoal.

sentences.text: —Buenos días, don —dice Karla.
sentences.english: "Good morning, sir," says Karla.

sentences.text: ¿A cómo la leña?
sentences.english: "How much is the firewood?"

sentences.text: —Una carga de leña, cien lempiras —contesta el hombre.
sentences.english: "A load of firewood, one hundred lempiras," answers the man.

sentences.text: —¿Y el carbón?
sentences.english: "And the charcoal?"

sentences.text: ¿Cuánto cuestan los sacos?
sentences.english: "How much are the sacks?"

sentences.text: —El saco pequeño, treinta, y el grande, cincuenta —dice el hombre.
sentences.english: "The small sack, thirty, and the big one, fifty," says the man.

sentences.text: —Dos sacos grandes y una carga de leña, ¿cuánto sale? —pregunta Ana.
sentences.english: "Two big sacks and a load of firewood, how much does that come to?" asks Ana.

sentences.text: —Doscientos, pero para usted le hago un descuento —dice el hombre.
sentences.english: "Two hundred, but I'll give you a discount," says the man.

sentences.text: —Ciento ochenta, y nos llevamos también los pedazos pequeños que tiene en el carro —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "A hundred and eighty, and we'll also take the small pieces you have in the car," says Ana.

sentences.text: —Ciento ochenta y cinco, y no regateen más —termina el hombre.
sentences.english: "A hundred and eighty-five, and don't haggle any more," the man finishes.

sentences.text: Karla saca los billetes, y Ana cuenta los sacos de carbón antes de pagar.
sentences.english: Karla takes out the notes, and Ana counts the sacks of charcoal before paying.

sentences.text: Entre las dos suben la carga de leña al carro del hombre.
sentences.english: Between the two of them they lift the load of firewood onto the man's car.

sentences.text: La leña y el carbón son para cocinar mañana en la cocina de la escuela, que todavía tiene una estufa vieja.
sentences.english: The firewood and the charcoal are for cooking tomorrow in the school kitchen, which still has an old stove.

sentences.text: La estufa sólo sirve con carbón, y la madera sirve para calentar el agua.
sentences.english: The stove only works with charcoal, and the wood is for heating the water.

sentences.text: Sin la estufa no hay fiesta, y sin carbón no hay estufa.
sentences.english: Without the stove there is no party, and without charcoal there is no stove.

sections.title: El pastel, la miel y los globos

sentences.text: Para el pastel hace falta harina, huevos, azúcar y miel.
sentences.english: For the cake you need flour, eggs, sugar and honey.

sentences.text: Karla compra una botella de miel, de las que se venden en la esquina del mercado.
sentences.english: Karla buys a bottle of honey, one of those sold at the corner of the market.

sentences.text: —¿Y por qué es tan cara, don? —pregunta Karla.
sentences.english: "And why is it so dear, sir?" asks Karla.

sentences.text: —Porque la miel no se hace sola, y las abejas trabajan mucho —contesta el señor.
sentences.english: "Because honey does not make itself, and the bees work a lot," answers the man.

sentences.text: Después van a un puesto donde venden globos de todos los colores.
sentences.english: Then they go to a stall where they sell balloons of every colour.

sentences.text: Los globos son baratos, y los hay de todas las formas.
sentences.english: The balloons are cheap, and there are all shapes.

sentences.text: Karla compra veinte globos, una piñata en forma de estrella y un paquete de velas.
sentences.english: Karla buys twenty balloons, a piñata in the shape of a star and a packet of candles.

sentences.text: Ana mira la piñata y se acuerda de su cumpleaños de niña.
sentences.english: Ana looks at the piñata and remembers her birthdays as a girl.

sentences.text: —Mi mamá no tenía dinero para una piñata, pero hacía una con papel y con maíz —cuenta Ana.
sentences.english: "My mother had no money for a piñata, but she made one with paper and corn," Ana tells her.

sentences.text: —Y ahora Nico va a tener una de estrella, y los chiquitines del pueblo van a pelear por los dulces —dice Karla.
sentences.english: "And now Nico will have a star one, and the little ones from the town will fight over the sweets," says Karla.

sentences.text: —Qué niño más inteligente es Nico, ¿verdad? —dice Karla.
sentences.english: "What a clever boy Nico is, isn't he?" says Karla.

sentences.text: —Ya aprendió a leer en dos idiomas, y le encanta hablar con los chiquitines de la escuela —contesta Ana.
sentences.english: "He has already learned to read in two languages, and he loves talking to the little ones at school," answers Ana.

sentences.text: —Dicen que es demasiado inteligente para su edad, pero yo creo que sólo pregunta mucho.
sentences.english: "They say he is too clever for his age, but I think he just asks a lot of questions."

sentences.text: Con las bolsas llenas, Karla y Ana buscan un carro que las lleve de vuelta.
sentences.english: With their bags full, Karla and Ana look for a car to take them back.

sentences.text: Un señor las deja subir a su carro, entre sacos de maíz y pedazos de madera.
sentences.english: A man lets them climb into his car, among sacks of corn and pieces of wood.

sentences.text: La madera es para el carbón, y los sacos de maíz son para la escuela.
sentences.english: The wood is for the charcoal, and the sacks of corn are for the school.

sentences.text: —¿Y el helado? —pregunta Karla.
sentences.english: "And the ice cream?" asks Karla.

sentences.text: ¿Dónde lo vamos a guardar?
sentences.english: "Where are we going to keep it?"

sentences.text: —Compramos el helado mañana temprano, para que no se derrita —contesta Ana.
sentences.english: "We'll buy the ice cream early tomorrow, so that it does not melt," answers Ana.

sentences.text: —¿Y qué helado quiere Nico? —pregunta Karla.
sentences.english: "And what ice cream does Nico want?" asks Karla.

sentences.text: —De mango, claro, como el jugo —dice Ana.
sentences.english: "Mango, of course, like the juice," says Ana.

sentences.text: —Y el jugo lo preparamos mañana con las naranjas, la piña, el mango y los limones.
sentences.english: "And we'll make the juice tomorrow with the oranges, the pineapple, the mango and the lemons."

sentences.text: —A ver, miremos la lista —dice Karla—: piñas, limones, aguacates, la yuca, naranjas, mango, huevos y pollos.
sentences.english: "Let's go over the list," says Karla: "pineapples, lemons, avocados, yuca, oranges, mango, eggs and chickens."

sentences.text: —Y el pastel, los globos y la piñata —dice Ana—.
sentences.english: "And the cake, the balloons and the piñata," says Ana.

sentences.text: —El pastel lo hacemos nosotras mañana, con la miel y con harina de la buena.
sentences.english: "We'll make the cake ourselves tomorrow, with the honey and with good flour."

sentences.text: —Y para los mayores, un café fino con pastel.
sentences.english: "And for the grown-ups, a fine coffee with cake."

sentences.text: —Y los aguacates los comemos con la yuca frita, como hace mi tía.
sentences.english: "And we'll eat the avocados with fried yuca, the way my aunt makes it."

sentences.text: —Con yuca y con aguacates no necesitamos mucho más.
sentences.english: "With yuca and avocados we don't need much more."

sentences.text: Karla mira la plaza que queda atrás, llena de colores y de gritos.
sentences.english: Karla watches the square staying behind, full of colours and shouts.

sentences.text: —Qué hermosa es la plaza, ¿verdad?
sentences.english: "How beautiful the square is, isn't it?"

sentences.text: —Sí, y cada sábado parece más hermosa, aunque cada sábado pagamos un poco más.
sentences.english: "Yes, and each Saturday it seems more beautiful, although each Saturday we pay a little more."

sentences.text: Ana se ríe, y Karla también, y el carro sigue por el camino de tierra hasta la clínica.
sentences.english: Ana laughs, and Karla does too, and the car goes on along the dirt road to the clinic.

sentences.text: La tarde antes de su cumpleaños, Nico tiene examen de vocabulario, y su tía Ana lo repasa con él en una banca de la plaza.
sentences.english: The afternoon before his birthday, Nico has a vocabulary exam, and his aunt Ana reviews it with him on a bench in the square.

sentences.text: —A ver, Nico: ¿qué es una donación? —Es lo que dan los voluntarios a los damnificados y a las víctimas.
sentences.english: "Let's see, Nico: what is a donation?" "It is what volunteers give to the victims and to those affected."

sentences.text: —¿Qué agua es potable? —La que lleva cloro. Hay que limpiar bien el criadero donde nacen los zancudos.
sentences.english: "Which water is drinkable?" "The one that has chlorine. You have to clean well the breeding place where mosquitoes are born."

sentences.text: —¿Y qué se hace inmediatamente? —Lo que no puede esperar. Un niño agitado, o inquieto, necesita calma inmediatamente.
sentences.english: "And what is done immediately?" "What cannot wait. A child who is agitated, or restless, needs calm immediately."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo describís un relámpago? —De repente, una luz que cae de una nube. Los relámpagos asustan, pero pasan.
sentences.english: "How do you describe lightning?" "Suddenly, a light that falls from a cloud. Flashes of lightning scare, but they pass."

sentences.text: —¿Qué hay en un mural de plástico? —Colores, una crónica del desastre y un pañuelo para limpiar el pincel.
sentences.english: "What is there in a plastic mural?" "Colors, a chronicle of the disaster and a handkerchief to clean the brush."

sentences.text: —¿Se necesita preparación para una campaña? —Sí, pasos concretos, y alguien que sepa justificar cada gasto. Con paciencia y más paciencia.
sentences.english: "Is preparation needed for a campaign?" "Yes, concrete steps, and somebody who knows how to justify each expense. With patience and more patience."

sentences.text: —¿Qué lleva una clínica en la puerta? —Una entrada, una salida y un cartel que dice «prohibido fumar».
sentences.english: "What does a clinic have at the door?" "An entrance, an exit and a sign that says 'no smoking'."

sentences.text: —¿Es gratuita la consulta? —Sí, es gratuita, pero hay que llenar una ficha con apellido, identidad y firma.
sentences.english: "Is the consultation free?" "Yes, it is free, but you have to fill out a card with surname, identity and signature."

sentences.text: —¿Y si es urgente? —Se hace formalmente después. La enfermera pone el suero, o la ambulancia llega enseguida.
sentences.english: "And if it is urgent?" "It is done formally afterwards. The nurse puts in the serum, or the ambulance arrives right away."

sentences.text: —¿Qué lleva un voluntario comprometido? —Guantes, un carné, una gota de cloro en cada litro y una cucharada de azúcar para el café.
sentences.english: "What does a committed volunteer carry?" "Gloves, an ID, a drop of chlorine in each liter and a spoonful of sugar for the coffee."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo trabaja un voluntario enterado? —Con rigor, con una dosis de buen humor y con la lista de cada día. Todo lo que no es habitual, lo avisa.
sentences.english: "How does an informed volunteer work?" "With rigor, with a dose of good humor and with the list of each day. Anything that is not usual, he reports."

sentences.text: —¿Dónde se sientan los espectadores? —En las butacas iluminadas. La sala es excelente, pero las latas de comida no se abren allí.
sentences.english: "Where do the spectators sit?" "In the lit seats. The room is excellent, but the cans of food are not opened there."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo está un cuarto sucio? —Sucio, no limpio. Y un cuarto iluminado es lo contrario de uno oscuro.
sentences.english: "How is a dirty room?" "Dirty, not clean. And a lit room is the opposite of a dark one."

sentences.text: —Muy bien. Ahora la parte de la montaña: ¿qué es un sendero? —Un camino pequeño en un terreno de cerros, entre la milpa y el corral.
sentences.english: "Very well. Now the mountain part: what is a path?" "A small road on hilly ground, between the cornfield and the corral."

sentences.text: —¿Quién es una viuda? —Una mujer cuyo marido ya murió. Y un solterón es un hombre que nunca se casó y que a veces es melancólico.
sentences.english: "Who is a widow?" "A woman whose husband has already died. And a confirmed bachelor is a man who never married and who is sometimes melancholy."

sentences.text: —¿Y un pretexto? —Una razón falsa. Un rumor puede ser un pretexto, y una tragedia puede ser una molestia o una grosería, según quién la cuente.
sentences.english: "And a pretext?" "A false reason. A rumor can be a pretext, and a tragedy can be a nuisance or a rudeness, depending on who tells it."

sentences.text: —¿Qué hace un sobrino? —Visita a su tío, y una vez lo complicó todo con una pregunta, pero la hizo con ritmo y con disposición.
sentences.english: "What does a nephew do?" "He visits his uncle, and once he complicated everything with a question, but he asked it with rhythm and with willingness."

sentences.text: —¿Puede ser interesante una autoridad? —Puede, si no estalla de ira: yo no la tolero cuando es una grosería, pero la tolero cuando es una voz justa.
sentences.english: "Can an authority be interesting?" "It can, if it does not burst with anger: I don't tolerate it when it is rudeness, but I tolerate it when it is a just voice."

sentences.text: —Y al final, ¿cómo se contuvieron los presos? —Se contuvieron sin destruir nada. Contuvieron el miedo, y después los trasladaron a la escuela.
sentences.english: "And in the end, how did the prisoners hold themselves back?" "They held themselves back without destroying anything. They held back their fear, and afterwards they were moved to the school."

sentences.text: —¿Qué dice un difunto cuando algo es evidente? —Nada. Pero los vivos nos enteramos de lo que es moral y de lo que es una profunda tristeza, en una casa amplia o pequeña.
sentences.english: "What does a deceased person say when something is evident?" "Nothing. But the living find out what is moral and what is a deep sadness, in a wide house or a small one."

sentences.text: Ana cerró el cuaderno y sonrió. —Mañana, en tu fiesta, solo vas a necesitar una piñata y un pastel.
sentences.english: Ana closed the notebook and smiled. "Tomorrow, at your party, you will only need a piñata and a cake."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo se trata a los niños inquietos y a los niños agitados? —Con mucha paciencia, mija. Hay que vaciar los criaderos y vaciar también el miedo.
sentences.english: "How do you treat restless children and agitated children?" "With a lot of patience, dear. You have to empty the breeding places and empty the fear too."

sentences.text: —¿Qué exige el trabajo con un preso? —Respeto. No se pregunta por lo que había acontecido; se escucha, en una sala iluminada y tranquila.
sentences.english: "What does working with a prisoner demand?" "Respect. One does not ask about what had happened; one listens, in a lit and quiet room."

sentences.text: —¿Cómo estaba la señora alarmada? —Aterrada. Me enteré de que no había dormido, y de que completamente sola, en el interior de su casa, había rezado.
sentences.english: "How was the alarmed lady?" "Terrified. I found out that she had not slept, and that, completely alone, in the interior of her house, she had prayed."

sentences.text: —¿Qué se regala en una fiesta? —Un ramo de flores, un par de zapatos, o una chala de maíz con dulce, si la tía no tiene más.
sentences.english: "What is given at a party?" "A bouquet of flowers, a pair of shoes, or a corn husk with sweet, if the aunt has nothing else."
